title: Inositol Hexakisphosphate Promotes Open Pore State in HIV Capsid Protein Lattice by Reconfiguring Subunit Contacts.
authors: Knelissen, Yari Katar; Escrig, Judith; Macke, Amanda C; Sudhakar, Sruthi; Dominguez-Zotes, Santos; Maity, Sourav; Mateu, Mauricio G; Perilla, Juan R; Roos, Wouter H; Valbuena, Alejandro
one_liner_zh: 该文结合高速原子力显微镜和恒pH分子动力学模拟，揭示IP6通过重构亚基接触稳定HIV衣壳蛋白六聚体孔道开放态，属于蛋白质结构动态与MD模拟计算研究，与课题高度相关。
abstract: The mature human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1) capsid is composed of approximately 250 capsid protein hexamers, each containing a central pore delimited by a beta-hairpin and an alpha-helix from each monomer. The cellular metabolite inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6) binds this pore and modulates translocation of nucleoside triphosphates into the capsid, where they fuel reverse transcription of the viral genome. However, the mechanism by which IP6 modulates the pore conformation is poorly understood. Averaged structural models of the HIV-1 capsid protein lattice have shed some light on this mechanism but lack information on the dynamic behavior of individual hexamers that could provide deeper mechanistic insights. Here we visualized in real time by high-speed atomic force microscopy the asynchronous motions of individual hexamer pores in the presence or absence of IP6, identifying dynamic transitions between two major states. Quantitative analysis enabled estimation of the IP6-induced pore conformations and populations. Constant-pH molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that IP6 induces contact rewiring at the pore entrance, stabilizing the open state through coordinated rearrangement of intersubunit interactions. Consistently, mechanical fatigue assays show that IP6 markedly enhances the resistance of the capsid lattice to mechanical fatigue, revealing its role as a mechanically stabilized nanomaterial. Together, these results establish IP6 as a proviral regulator that couples nanoscale pore dynamics, intersubunit contact reconfiguration, and mechanical resilience of the HIV-1 capsid, providing a unified mechanistic framework for its role in viral replication.
abstract_zh: 成熟的人类免疫缺陷病毒（HIV-1）衣壳由约250个衣壳蛋白六聚体组成，每个六聚体包含一个由每个单体中的β-发夹和α-螺旋界定的中央孔道。细胞代谢物六磷酸肌醇（IP6）结合该孔道，并调节核苷三磷酸向衣壳内的转运，这些核苷三磷酸在衣壳内驱动病毒基因组的逆转录。然而，IP6调节孔道构象的机制尚不清楚。HIV-1衣壳蛋白晶格的平均结构模型已对此机制提供了一些见解，但缺乏单个六聚体动态行为的信息，而这些信息可能提供更深入的机制性认识。在此，我们通过高速原子力显微镜实时观察了在存在或不存在IP6的情况下单个六聚体孔道的异步运动，识别出两种主要状态之间的动态转变。定量分析使得能够估计IP6诱导的孔道构象及其群体分布。恒定pH分子动力学模拟进一步揭示，IP6诱导孔道入口处的接触重连，通过亚基间相互作用的协调重排稳定开放状态。一致地，机械疲劳实验表明，IP6显著增强衣壳晶格对机械疲劳的抵抗力，揭示其作为机械稳定纳米材料的作用。综合来看，这些结果确立了IP6作为一种前病毒调节因子，耦合了HIV-1衣壳的纳米尺度孔道动态、亚基间接触重构和机械韧性，为其在病毒复制中的作用提供了统一的机制框架。
